files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller's checklist

Owner: B. Okafor. Complete in sequence; no skips.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, propose one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 and paying in July; some months all runs pay in-month. If such a period exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule and supporting contracts. Check the GL first to avoid a duplicate. If it has not been posted, book June amortization as ONE combined journal entry. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month each prepaid item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after verifying the GL to ensure it has not already been recorded.
5. Test June vendor-bill expense coding by comparing the bill documents with the GL. Reclass anything miscoded to the correct expense account.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, after items 1-5 have been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Maple & Main Retail Co. began in 2018 when two former specialty-store coworkers started assembling practical gift boxes from a shared worktable. They believed online shopping could still feel personal: useful products, thoughtful presentation, and a note from an actual human being. Early word of mouth turned the side project into a focused ecommerce operation.

Today, the company sells home-office accessories, small household goods, seasonal gift sets, stationery, and curated care packages. Its assortment leans toward approachable design and products that are easy to give, ship, and use. Orders move through a compact fulfillment space where the merchandising and operations teams work within easy shouting distance of one another.

The team has a hands-on flavor. Buyers trade packaging ideas with warehouse staff, customer-service notes regularly influence product descriptions, and marketing is happiest when testing a fresh campaign theme. Leadership keeps the culture informal but expects clean handoffs and dependable follow-through.

The current focus is steady execution: refining the catalog, improving the online storefront, strengthening vendor relationships, and making fulfillment smoother during busy selling periods. Maple & Main Retail Co. remains an ordinary operating business, balancing day-to-day customer needs with measured plans for continued growth.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Give Maple & Main Retail Co. a warmer, more recognizable point of view without losing the practical tone customers already trust. The refresh should show up consistently across the storefront, email, packaging inserts, and partner materials.

## Priorities

- Tighten the visual system and simplify core brand messages.
- Build seasonal campaigns around gifting, useful home goods, and workday upgrades.
- Run two educational webinars per quarter, using product demonstrations and practical gift-planning themes rather than hard-sell presentations.
- Pilot a co-marketing program with a complementary partner whose audience overlaps with ours.
- Develop reusable photography, short-form video, and customer stories for organic and paid channels.
- Improve post-purchase messaging so first-time buyers have a clear reason to return.

## Quarter focus

### Q3

Complete the brand refresh, update campaign templates, test webinar formats, and identify a partner for the pilot. Establish a simple reporting rhythm for channel performance and content reuse.

### Q4

Apply the refreshed brand to seasonal merchandising, expand the strongest webinar concept, and launch the partner campaign. Coordinate email, social, and storefront storytelling around a shared editorial calendar.

## Open items

Channel mix and final scope remain subject to the Q2 close and team capacity. Owners and production deadlines will be assigned after leadership review.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# Notes from the previous chair

B. Okafor — a few practical things I learned the long way:

- The bank's own service fees and charges usually appear near the end of the statement. They are historically picked up and booked during close, so do not assume the ledger already has them.
- Please give June vendor-bill coding a real look. A couple of expenses may be sitting in the wrong accounts, and the documents in `bills/` are authoritative if the GL description is vague.
- The budget was fixed early, at the start of the quarter. The one-off June items were never planned, and they are generally the explanation for the larger budget-to-actual variances.
- For payroll timing, trust the register. The pay date for the back-half run varies: in some months it falls in the next month, but in other months every run pays in-month. Do not infer the timing from prior closes.
